calls.head: Nowhere to hide for Thompson
calls.body: At home, the Panthers keep sending Lundell’s line (Luostarinen, Lundell and Vilmanis) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Paul Maurice has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Sabres’ first line is Benson, Kulich and Thompson.

calls.head: Lyon’s hold on the Panthers won’t last
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Lyon has been a wall against the Panthers, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Panthers finally get to him.

calls.body: The Sabres’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Panthers’ power play is one of the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Sabres tonight. The Sabres take a lot of penalties and the Panthers draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Bennett lights the lamp for a hat trick
paras: Sam Bennett opened the scoring for the Panthers early in the first, but Jiří Kulich tied it 1-1 for Buffalo midway through the period. Jack Quinn gave the Sabres the lead early in the second. Bennett scored his second of the night just 18 seconds later to tie it 2-2, and the goal stood after the Sabres challenged for goalie interference. Bennett completed his hat trick shorthanded just 48 seconds into the third to put the Panthers ahead 3-2. Tage Thompson made it 3-3 for Buffalo midway through the period, but the Sabres didn’t score again. Sandis Vilmanis put the Panthers ahead for good with a little over three minutes left.

The Sabres were outshot 30-19, but their looks were better, and the chances came out about even. Jacob Markström made 16 saves for the Panthers, and Alex Lyon stopped 26 of 30 at the other end. The Cats improved to 13-8-3, fifth in the Atlantic, while the Sabres dropped to 9-10-4, sixth in the Atlantic.
